nnn - Supercharge your productivity!

`nnn` (_n³_) is a full-featured terminal file manager. It's tiny, nearly 0-config and incredibly fast. It is designed to be unobtrusive with smart workflows to match the trains of thought. `nnn` can analyze disk usage, batch rename, launch apps and pick files. The plugin repository has tons of plugins to extend the capabilities further e.g. live previews, (un)mount disks, find & list, file/dir diff, upload files. Runs on the Pi, Termux (Android), Linux, macOS, BSD, Haiku, Cygwin, WSL, across DEs or a strictly CLI env. ## Features - Quality - Privacy-aware (no unconfirmed user data collection) - POSIX-compliant - Highly optimized code - Frugal - Typically needs less than 3.5MB resident memory - Works with 8 colors (and xterm 256 colors) - Disk-IO sensitive (few disk reads and writes) - No FPU usage (all integer maths, even for file size) - Minimizes screen refresh with fast line redraws - Tiny binary (typically around 100KB) - 1-column mode for smaller terminals and form factors - Portable - Language-agnostic plugins - Static binary available (no need to install) - Minimal library deps, easy to compile - No config file, minimal config with sensible defaults - Plugin to backup configuration - Widely available on many packagers - Touch enabled, handheld-friendly shortcuts - Unicode support - Modes - Light (default), detail - Disk usage analyzer (block/apparent) - File picker - Navigation - Filter with automatic dir entry on unique match - *Type-to-nav* (turbo navigation/always filter) mode - Jump to an entry with visible relative offset - Contexts (_aka_ tabs/workspaces) with custom colors - Sessions, bookmarks, mark and visit a dir - Remote mounts (needs `sshfs`, `rclone`) - Familiar shortcuts (arrows, ~, -, @), quick look-up - `cd` on quit (*easy* shell integration) - Proceed to next file on file open and selection - Search - Instant filtering with *search-as-you-type* - Fuzzy, regex and string (default) filters - Subtree search plugin to open or edit files - Sort - Ordered pure numeric names by default (visit `/proc`) - Case-insensitive version (_aka_ natural) sort - By name, access/change/mod (default) time, size, extn - Reverse sort - Directory-specific ordering - Mimes - Preview hovered files in FIFO-based previewer - Open with desktop opener or specify a custom opener - File-specific colors (or minimal _dirs in context color_) - Icons and Emojis support (customize and compile-in) - Plugin for image, video and audio thumbnails - Create, list, extract (to), mount (FUSE based) archives - Option to open all text files in `$EDITOR` - Convenience - Detailed file stats and mime information - Run plugins and custom commands with hotkeys - FreeDesktop compliant trash utility integration - Cross-dir file/all/range selection - Create (with parents), rename, duplicate files and dirs - Create new file or directory (tree) on startup - Batch renamer for selection or dir - List input stream of file paths from stdin or plugin - Copy (as), move (as), delete, archive, link selection - Easily copy, move paths in system clipboard to current dir - Dir updates, notification on `cp`, `mv`, `rm` completion - Copy file paths to system clipboard on select - Launch apps, run commands, spawn a shell, toggle exe - Access context paths/files at prompt or spawned shell - Lock terminal after configurable idle timeout - Capture and show output of a program in help screen - Basic support for screen readers and braille displays ## Usage Don't memorize! Arrows, /, q suffice. Tab creates and/or cycles contexts. ? lists shortcuts. For detailed usage instructions, command-line options, and configuration information, please refer to the man page (`man nnn`) or visit the project Wiki. ## Installation `nnn` is available on many package managers. Install it using your distribution's package manager, or download a pre-built static binary. Common installation methods: - **Arch Linux**: `pacman -S nnn` - **Debian/Ubuntu**: `apt install nnn` - **Fedora**: `dnf install nnn` - **macOS (Homebrew)**: `brew install nnn` - **FreeBSD**: `pkg install nnn` For more installation options and detailed instructions, visit the project Wiki. ## License BSD 2-Clause License Copyright © 2016-2026 Arun Prakash Jana and contributors See LICENSE file for full license text. ===

.Dd Feb 14, 2026
.Dt NNN 1
.Os
.Sh NAME
.Nm nnn
.Nd The unorthodox terminal file manager.
.Sh SYNOPSIS
.Nm
.Op Ar -aAcCdDeEfgHJKnQrRSuUVxz0h
.Op Ar -b key
.Op Ar -F val
.Op Ar -l val
.Op Ar -p file
.Op Ar -P key
.Op Ar -s name
.Op Ar -t secs
.Op Ar -T key
.Op Ar PATH
.Sh DESCRIPTION
.Nm
.Pq Nnn's Not Noice
is a performance-optimized, feature-packed terminal file manager
with seamless desktop integration, simplified navigation,
.Em type-to-nav
mode with dir auto-enter, disk usage analyzer mode, bookmarks,
contexts, application launcher, familiar navigation shortcuts,
subshell spawning and much more. It remains a simple and
efficient file manager that stays out of your way.
.Pp
.Nm
opens the current working directory if
.Ar PATH
is not specified. If
.Ar PATH
is specified and it exists,
.Nm
will open it. If the
.Ar PATH
doesn't exist and ends with a \fB/\fR,
.Nm
will attempt to create the directory tree and open it. Otherwise,
.Ar PATH
is considered a path to a regular file and
.Nm
attempts to create the complete directory tree to the file, open
the parent directory and prompt to create the new file in it with
the base filename.

full documentation or run

with the

import subprocess, os, sys

def run(args, stdin=None, env=None, timeout=5):
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, env=env)
        return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        return "TIMEOUT", e.stdout, e.stderr

for args in [["-h"], ["--help"], ["-V"], ["--version"], ["-v"], ["-H"], ["-x"]]:
    rc,out,err = run(args)
    print(f"=== args={args} rc={rc} ===")
    print("STDOUT:", repr(out[:4000]))
    print("STDERR:", repr(err[:4000]))
    print()

import subprocess

def run(args, stdin=None, timeout=5):
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        return "TIMEOUT", str(e.stdout), str(e.stderr)

# Need to capture exact help text bytes including newlines
p = subprocess.run(["./executable","-h"], capture_output=True)
print(repr(p.stdout))
print("---stderr---", repr(p.stderr), "rc", p.returncode)
# check -V
p = subprocess.run(["./executable","-V"], capture_output=True)
print(repr(p.stdout), repr(p.stderr), p.returncode)
# check invalid
p = subprocess.run(["./executable","-Z"], capture_output=True)
print("invalid -Z stdout:", repr(p.stdout[:200]), "stderr:", repr(p.stderr), "rc", p.returncode)
# check missing arg: does it print usage to stdout? yes?
p = subprocess.run(["./executable","-b"], capture_output=True)
print("missing -b stdout len", len(p.stdout), "stderr", repr(p.stderr), "rc", p.returncode)
# check argv0 in error? It prints ./executable: ...
# What if invoked via different name? symlink?
import os
os.symlink("/tmp", "/tmp/linktest") if False else None
# Test F 2 case: why no err? Let's see exit code and outputs
for a in [["-F","2"],["-F","2","/tmp"],["-F","9"],["-t","-5"],["-l","-5"]]:
    p = subprocess.run(["./executable"]+a, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
    print(a, "rc", p.returncode, "out", repr(p.stdout[:200]), "err", repr(p.stderr[:200]))

def run_pty(args, cwd="/tmp", inputs=None, timeout=3, env=None, cols=80, rows=24):
    import os, pty, subprocess, select, time
    EXE=os.path.abspath("executable")
    # create pty pair
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    # set winsize?
    import struct, fcntl, termios
    # set size 24x80
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0))
    e = os.environ.copy()
    e["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
    if env:
        e.update(env)
    p = subprocess.Popen([EXE]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, cwd=cwd, env=e, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    # nonblocking?
    import fcntl as fc
    flags = fc.fcntl(master, fc.F_GETFL)
    fc.fcntl(master, fc.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    output = b""

    # if inputs is list of (delay, bytes), send them
    # simple: wait a bit, capture, then send 'q'
    time.sleep(0.5)
    # read available
    def drain():
        nonlocal output
        try:
            while True:
                r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], 0.1)
                if not r:
                    break
                try:
                    d=os.read(master, 4096)
                    if not d:
                        break
                    output+=d
                except OSError:
                    break
        except Exception as ex:
            print(ex)
    drain()
    # send inputs
    if inputs:
        for delay, data in inputs:
            time.sleep(delay)
            os.write(master, data)
            time.sleep(0.3)
            drain()
    else:

        try:
            os.write(master, b"q")
        except: pass
        time.sleep(0.5)
        drain()
    # try to wait
    try:
        p.wait(timeout=2)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        p.kill()
        try:
            p.wait(timeout=1)
        except: pass
    # drain remaining
    time.sleep(0.2)
    drain()
    os.close(master)
    return p.returncode, output

def run_pty(args, cwd="/tmp", sends=[b"q"], wait_each=0.6, init_wait=0.8):

    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 24, 80, 0, 0))
    e=os.environ.copy()
    e["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
    # ensure clean env for nnn? unset NNN_*?
    for k in list(e.keys()):
        if k.startswith("NNN_"):
            del e[k]
    p=subprocess.Popen([EXE]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, cwd=cwd, env=e)
    os.close(slave)
    time.sleep(init_wait)
    import fcntl as fc
    flags=fc.fcntl(master, fc.F_GETFL)
    fc.fcntl(master, fc.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    out=b""
    def drain():
        nonlocal out
        try:
            while True:
                try:
                    d=os.read(master, 16384)
                    if not d: break
                    out+=d
                except BlockingIOError:
                    break
                except OSError:
                    break
        except: pass
    drain()
    for s in sends:
        try: os.write(master, s)
        except: pass
        time.sleep(wait_each)
        drain()
    try:
        p.wait(timeout=1)
    except:
        p.kill()
        try: p.wait(timeout=1)
        except: pass
    drain()
    try: os.close(master)
    except: pass
    return p.returncode, out

EXE=os.path.abspath("executable")
def run(args, stdin=None, env=None):
    e=os.environ.copy()
    if env is not None:
        e.update(env)
    # stdin: None = inherit, "PIPE" = pipe empty, "DATA" = pipe with data
    inp = stdin
    p=subprocess.run([EXE]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5, env=e)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr

print("TERM=", os.environ.get("TERM"))
for term in ["dumb", "unknown", "xterm", "xterm-256color", None]:
    env = {}
    if term is None:
        # unset TERM
        e=os.environ.copy()
        if "TERM" in e: del e["TERM"]
        p=subprocess.run([EXE], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5, env=e)
        print(f"TERM unset => rc={p.returncode} out={repr(p.stdout[:100])} err={repr(p.stderr[:200])}")
    else:
        env={"TERM": term}
        rc,out,err=run([], env=env)
        print(f"TERM={term} inherit stdin => rc={rc} out={repr(out[:100])} err={repr(err[:200])}")

# Now with stdin piped
for term in ["dumb", "xterm-256color"]:
    e=os.environ.copy()
    e["TERM"]=term
    p=subprocess.run([EXE], input="", capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5, env=e)

import subprocess, os, tempfile, shutil
EXE=os.path.abspath("executable")
def run(args, cwd, term="dumb"):
    e=os.environ.copy(); e["TERM"]=term
    p=subprocess.run([EXE]+args, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True, timeout=5, cwd=cwd, env=e)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr

tmp=tempfile.mkdtemp()
print("tmp", tmp)
# ensure empty
for args in [[tmp+"/newdir1/"], [tmp+"/newdir2/sub/"], [tmp+"/newfile1.txt"], ["newdir3/",], ["newfile2.txt"]]:
    # cleanup first
    import pathlib
    print(f"\n--- args {args} cwd={tmp} ---")
    rc,out,err=run(args, cwd=tmp)
    print(f"rc={rc} out={repr(out[:100])} err={repr(err[:100])}")
    print("  ls:", os.listdir(tmp))
    # cleanup
    for p in os.listdir(tmp):
        pp=os.path.join(tmp,p)
        if p.startswith("new"):
            if os.path.isdir(pp):
                shutil.rmtree(pp)
            else:
                os.remove(pp)
PY

import os, subprocess, time, struct, fcntl, termios, pty, re
EXE=os.path.abspath("executable")
def run_pty(args, cwd="/workspace"):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 24, 80, 0, 0))
    e=os.environ.copy(); e["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
    p=subprocess.Popen([EXE]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, cwd=cwd, env=e)
    os.close(slave)
    time.sleep(0.7)
    import fcntl as fc
    flags=fc.fcntl(master, fc.F_GETFL)
    fc.fcntl(master, fc.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    out=b""
    def drain():
        nonlocal out
        try:
            while True:
                try:
                    d=os.read(master, 16384)
                    if not d: break
                    out+=d
                except BlockingIOError: break
                except OSError: break
        except: pass
    drain()
    # send Down to select next file, then capture?
    # For now just send q
    try: os.write(master, b"q")
    except: pass
    time.sleep(0.5)
    drain()
    try: p.wait(timeout=1)
    except: p.kill()
    try: os.close(master)
    except: pass
    return out

out=run_pty([])
print(repr(out))
# Try to decode footer: look for 1/4 etc

def run_picker(sends, args_extra=[], cwd="/tmp"):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 24, 80, 0, 0))
    e=os.environ.copy(); e["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
    tmpfile=tempfile.mktemp()
    try: os.remove(tmpfile)
    except: pass
    args=args_extra+["-p", tmpfile]
    # need a test dir
    tmpdir=tempfile.mkdtemp()
    open(tmpdir+"/a.txt","w").write("a")
    open(tmpdir+"/b.txt","w").write("b")
    args.append(tmpdir)

    p=subprocess.Popen([EXE]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, cwd=cwd, env=e)

    flags=fc.fcntl(master, fc.F_GETFL)
    fc.fcntl(master, fc.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    out=b""
    def drain():
        nonlocal out
        try:
            while True:
                try:
                    d=os.read(master, 16384)
                    if not d: break
                    out+=d
                except BlockingIOError: break
                except OSError: break
        except: pass
    drain()
    for s in sends:
        try: os.write(master, s)
        except: pass

import os, subprocess, time, struct, fcntl, termios, pty
EXE=os.path.abspath("executable")
def run(sends, wait=0.6):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 24, 80, 0, 0))
    e=os.environ.copy(); e["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
    import tempfile
    tmp=tempfile.mkdtemp()
    open(tmp+"/a.txt","w").write("a")
    p=subprocess.Popen([EXE, tmp], stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, cwd="/tmp", env=e)
    os.close(slave)
    time.sleep(0.7)
    import fcntl as fc
    flags=fc.fcntl(master, fc.F_GETFL)
    fc.fcntl(master, fc.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    out=b""
    def drain():
        nonlocal out
        try:
            while True:
                try:
                    d=os.read(master, 16384)
                    if not d: break
                    out+=d
                except BlockingIOError: break
                except OSError: break
        except: pass
    drain()
    for s in sends:
        try: os.write(master, s)
        except: pass
        time.sleep(wait)
        drain()
        print("after", repr(s), "poll", p.poll(), "out len", len(out))
    try: p.wait(timeout=1)
    except: 
        print("still running, killing")
        p.kill()
    try: p.wait(timeout=1)
    except: pass
    print("final rc", p.returncode)
    print(repr(out[-2000:]))
    try: os.close(master)
    except: pass
    import shutil
    shutil.rmtree(tmp)

print("=== ? then wait, no q ===")
run([b"?"])
print("\n=== ? then q ===")
run([b"?", b"q"])
